target.title: fix(tts): contract speech requests hang on stalled endpoints
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where developers running the reusable OpenAI TTS contracts against a custom or local endpoint could wait indefinitely when the endpoint accepted the HTTP request but never returned response headers. Ordinary synthesis and telephony synthesis each had an independent unbounded request path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both contract fixture entry points now share one request helper built on the existing guarded fetch path. The helper applies the caller-provided speech timeout, limits configured-origin trust to the selected base URL hostname, and releases the guarded transport after headers arrive.

The production OpenAI TTS provider already follows this invariant, so this change stays inside the reusable contract fixture and does not change public APIs, configuration, schemas, or provider defaults.

## User Impact

TTS contract runs now fail within a bounded interval when an OpenAI-compatible endpoint stalls before headers, instead of hanging the test process indefinitely. This covers both normal audio synthesis and telephony synthesis.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the two loopback regressions failed with `ordinary synthesis did not time out` and `telephony synthesis did not time out` against servers that accepted requests but never wrote headers.
- On the submitted head (`f8f30becf2e9`), the complete TTS contract file passed 43/43 tests. The named fixture-path cases below use a 100 ms caller timeout and each server accepts exactly one request without writing headers.

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/plugins/contracts/tts.contract.test.ts --reporter verbose
✓ tts provider runtime contract > aborts stalled OpenAI 'ordinary synthesis' within the caller timeout 154ms
✓ tts provider runtime contract > aborts stalled OpenAI 'telephony synthesis' within the caller timeout 111ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests      43 passed (43)
```

- A separate bounded Node transport run opened one real loopback HTTP server per request shape. Each server accepted exactly one POST and deliberately returned no response headers. This is the redacted terminal excerpt; loopback ports are omitted.

```text
$ node --import tsx <loopback-timeout-proof>
head: f8f30becf2e9c36982d772b29db4d7b3b6120292
configured timeout: 1000ms

[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 1000ms (elapsed 1002ms) operation=fetchWithSsrFGuard url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/audio/speech
ordinary synthesis: requestCount=1, TimeoutError: request timed out, elapsed=1108ms

[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 1000ms (elapsed 1001ms) operation=fetchWithSsrFGuard url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/audio/speech
telephony synthesis: requestCount=1, TimeoutError: request timed out, elapsed=1030ms
```

- The mapped core extension facade boundary suite passed 4/4 tests, and focused formatting, lint, and diff whitespace checks passed.

Gateway startup is not applicable because the affected path is the reusable contract fixture transport rather than a gateway request path. The full contract suite directly executes both fixture entry points; the separate live loopback transcript records the guarded transport deadline over real TCP/HTTP connections.
